title: Jollof Rice
summary: A rich and spicy one-pot rice dish cooked in tomato stew, often served with fried plantain and grilled chicken.
instructions: Rinse the rice and set aside.
Blend tomatoes, onion, and pepper to make the base stew.
Heat oil in a pan, add tomato paste, and fry for 5 minutes.
Add blended tomato mixture and spices, then cook until thick.
Stir in rice and add water as needed.
Cover and simmer until rice is cooked and fluffy.

title: Banku and Tilapia
summary: A Ghanaian favorite made from fermented corn and cassava dough, served with grilled tilapia and spicy pepper sauce.
instructions: Mix corn and cassava dough with water and cook while stirring until smooth.
Grill seasoned tilapia until golden brown.
Blend tomatoes, onions, and chili to make pepper sauce.
Serve banku with tilapia and pepper sauce.

title: Waakye
summary: A flavorful rice and beans dish cooked with millet leaves, enjoyed with stew, spaghetti, and gari.
instructions: Boil beans with millet leaves until half cooked.
Add rice and baking soda, then cook together until soft.
Remove millet leaves and serve with stew, spaghetti, or gari.

title: Fufu and Light Soup
summary: Pounded cassava and plantain served with spicy light soup and meat or fish — a traditional Sunday delight.
instructions: Boil cassava and plantain until soft, then pound together until smooth.
Blend tomatoes, onion, and pepper for soup base.
Cook meat or fish with seasoning, add blended mixture, and simmer until done.
Serve hot with fufu.

title: Kelewele
summary: Spicy fried plantain seasoned with ginger, pepper, and cloves — a perfect street snack or side dish.
instructions: Peel and dice the plantains into bite-sized pieces.
Mix spices and coat the plantain pieces evenly.
Heat oil and fry until golden brown.
Serve hot as a snack or side dish.
